payload.vision_scope_stated: Complete. Vision inherited from se.vision with a one-line delta; to-be world written as a scene rather than an abstraction; goal system with three named conflicts and a ruled priority - reaching the owner outranks richness; Moore pitch in all five slots; scope as five ordered items; non-goals naming eight exclusions and where each went.
payload.problem_agreed: The delta is real, evidenced today, and the goal is worth having. A gate the owner was meant to bless reached nobody, and when a card finally did arrive its button could not be tapped - the owner read the error themselves: 'Expected URL scheme http or https but was answer.' The design document specifies a ladder whose top rung was built and verified in July and never ported; its own open-items list marked the rung that DID ship as never verified on a phone, and that is precisely the leg that failed. Meanwhile the other half works - the owner blessed i5d's release gate from their phone today, hash-bound, channel=phone - which proves the loop is worth completing rather than abandoning. The goal matters because the alternative is an owner who must return to the machine to unblock any unattended run, which defeats the point of running unattended.
payload.prior_art_positioned: Positioned against five alternatives, each shedding something: action buttons alone shed the reasoning; a tunnel to the machine sheds availability and is recorded as broken from a cloud sandbox; an artifact page sheds the answer leg because its CSP blocks outbound requests; plain chat sheds the away case; anonymous paste hosts shed rendering. Against prior work rather than hypotheticals: v1 already runs this shape - one browsable page per bless moment, the same page travelling as the ask's link, actions and page sharing one card - and se-v2-design §18 records the v2 transport as built and verified end to end, including a real phone tap. This iteration ports both rather than re-deciding either.
payload.success_measurable: Every need carries a pass line that a person could check, and three of them demand a real device rather than an assertion. A tap on a published card produces a recorded grant with channel=phone. The page opens on the phone and shows the gate's evidence fields, with the card titled as a GATE. Fetching the published key without the fragment returns ciphertext containing none of the brief's words. An induced publish failure appears in the record AND the gate still goes out with its actions. A human-blessed gate publishes even when the configuration changed after the board started.
payload.risks_logged: Six entries with owners and triggers: the secret leaving the machine (owner, high - and its claim was CORRECTED at the pressure test to say the fragment protects against the host, not against whoever holds the topic, since ntfy retains for about twelve hours); the token never being logged (agent); eventual consistency defeated by read-after-write (agent); the meta-risk that an unverified leg ships again, mitigated by ending the spike at a real tap (agent, high); the host going away, degrading rather than failing (owner); and silent degradation, pulled in as a requirement rather than left as a risk because it is what hid the current defect for a day (agent).
